findings.where: bar.py:1858-1871 (plan loop), 1964-1966 (supersede_record is called before the episodes run), 1990-1992 (only this session's it["supersedes"] reaches the record)
findings.problem: Rule R2's label is lost in two ways. (a) A `--supersede` run that is killed after the old record was moved aside: the next run of the same command finds no record at the path, so it["supersedes"] is None, the partial episodes are reused and the new record is written with no `supersedes` field. (b) A superseding record that holds an episode that failed to run: the next run of the same key runs that seed again and rewrites the record from `more = dict(extra)`, which does not carry the old record's `supersedes` over. In both cases a record made after a result is printed as if it were the registered one (R2: it must state `supersedes.reason` and be labelled "re-run after a result").
findings.fix: Make the label durable and carried: (1) in supersede_record write the returned dict to `<record>.superseded/<12 hex>.reason.json` before os.replace; (2) in the plan loop, when `<record>.superseded/` exists and the item has no supersedes of its own, rebuild it from those reason files; (3) at bar.py:1990 carry `old["supersedes"]` (and `old["replication_of"]` when --passed-of is absent) into `more` whenever a record of the same key is rewritten. Add a test: supersede, kill at the second episode, rerun, assert `supersedes.reason`; and supersede with one failed episode, rerun, assert it again.

findings.where: bar.py:1862-1870 and 1957-1961; the choice is asserted in tests/test_stage2_bar.py:932-941; rules_of at bar.py:305-318
findings.problem: A "not run" record is not treated as a finished record. When the set later lists the reference (a new freeze), the same command replaces the "not run" record by a "done" record with no stop, no `--supersede`, no copy and no `supersedes` field; a "not run" record whose key changed is also rewritten in place. "not run" is a registered outcome of the bar (H3), and A13 says a reference added by a later freeze is a change after a result whose records "replace no verdict of the registered set" and which is labelled so "in every record ... that uses it". bar.py has no such label at all (grep "change after a result" in bar.py: no match): a record only shows `set_freeze.index`. The builder decided this reading silently (the test comment says "a not run record holds no result").
findings.fix: (1) bar.py:1862: treat `old.status == "not run"` with `old.key != key` like a finished record: list it in `mismatched` unless `--supersede`, which keeps it under `<record>.superseded/` and writes `supersedes.reason`. (2) In condition_record and not_run_record, for every input file record the index of the first freeze whose manifest lists that (name, sha256), and when set.json labels that freeze or entry a change after a result (agree the field name with work package S) copy the label and its reason into the record's top level and into `_cell`. (3) Change the test at tests/test_stage2_bar.py:932-941 to expect the stop.

findings.where: run_75cm.sh:53-62 (step: exit 0 writes done/<name>) with bar.py:2756-2765 (main returns 0 whatever the records hold)
findings.problem: `bar run` exits 0 when episodes failed to run (an exception, an unreadable window, a lost worker, a failed trace write). The chain then writes the done-marker and never runs the unit again, so rule C8's "the same seed is run again on the next run of the same key" never happens for tier 1 and 2 of task 3 and for all of task 4 (only task 3's tier 10 repeats a command). A headline record can stay "incomplete" while the chain reports "all steps done".
findings.fix: In bar.main return a code of its own (4) when a record of the session holds `counts.errors > 0`, with one stderr line naming the records. In run_75cm.sh's step: on 4 run the same command once more (C8's second run, counted by the ledger); if it is 4 again write `done/<name>.incomplete`, log it and go on; `all` writes done/ALL only when no `.incomplete` marker exists. Extend test_a_step_of_the_chain_is_skipped_once_done_and_a_cut_goes_on with an exit-4 step.

findings.problem: The dirty flag counts the run's own uncommitted outputs. The registered run writes into stage2/runs/2026-11-15-75cm inside the repository, so from the second unit on every session records `dirty: true` and every record's `provenance.git.dirty_paths` lists every record, budget.json and summary written so far (hundreds of paths per record by the end). The flag no longer tells an edited source from the run's own files, and `sessions[]` holds no dirty paths at all. s2io.git_state has `own_outputs` for exactly this and the bar does not pass it. This cannot be repaired after state A (bar.py is in every key).
findings.fix: bar.py:1821: `git = s2io.git_state(own_outputs=[out])`; set `prov["git"] = git` (keeping plant.provenance()'s other fields); add `dirty_paths=git["dirty_paths"]` to `sess`. findings.where: bar.py:864-869 (set_crouch), called at 1807, 1651-1652, 2580; BarContext default at 787
findings.problem: The crouch that sets the track's LIPM frequency (rule B5) is read from set.json's top-level `crouch_frac`, which no freeze covers (the manifest lists entries only) and which nothing compares with the walk entries' own `crouch_frac` (in setio.WALK_SUBSET, so frozen through `entry_sha256`). A set.json whose value differs from the entries', by a builder's mistake or an edit after the freeze, is accepted: every later unit runs at another omega under the same `set_freeze.manifest_sha256`. Only an already finished record would stop the run (key mismatch).
findings.fix: Give set_crouch the set's documents and refuse (BarError naming both values) unless every walk entry the run plays (at least `nominal` and each condition's walk) records the same `crouch_frac` as set.json; or take the crouch from those frozen entries and refuse a set whose entries disagree. Add a test with set.json 0.05 against entries 0.03.

findings.where: run_75cm.sh:67-70 and 78 (r0_traces adds `--no-traces-for R0` under 1.5 GB free); bar.py:1671-1672 and 1826-1829
findings.problem: The registered chain drops the trace of every R0 episode when less than 1.5 GB is free. Rule R3 has no such exception: each episode's trace sha256 is in its record so that a reviewer can run the episode again and compare. With the flag the episode has no `trace` key at all, the choice depends on the disk at each step's start, and nothing records it: `no_traces_for` is in neither the record's sessions nor the summary's session, whose `traces` stays true.
findings.fix: Either remove r0_traces from the chain and stop with a clear message when the disk is short, or keep the hash: in run_episode always write the trace (to the trace path or a temporary file), record `trace = {sha256, rows, kept: false, reason}` and delete the file when it is not kept; and add `no_traces_for` to `sess` so that each record's session says so.
findings.evidence: scripts/e6_more.py 4 (no_traces_for=("R0",)): record.sessions[0] keys are attribute, blas_threads, block, commit, dirty, ended_at, id, procs, seeds_run, started_at, task, unit, versions, wall_s; "'no_traces' anywhere in the record: False | in the summary's session: False | session.traces: True". The design (D14) planned for about 4 GB free against 5 GB of traces, so the switch can trigger on another machine; this one has 21 GB free now.

findings.where: bar.py:1780-1781 (lock, sweep_tmp) and 1667-1682 (BarWorker.evaluate); s2io.Lock.stale judges the parent's pid only
findings.problem: After a SIGKILL of the runner its spawned workers live on, finish their episode and write a trace and a partial file into the run directory. The lock is stale the moment the parent dies, so a resume takes it over while those writers are active: its sweep_tmp can delete a temporary file an orphan is writing, and an orphan and a new worker of the same seed write the same `<seed>.npz.tmp`. The ledger also counts the repeated episode once. I saw no wrong record in three immediate resumes; the window is a few milliseconds per episode.
findings.fix: In BarWorker.__init__, when `multiprocessing.parent_process()` is not None, start a daemon thread that joins the parent and calls `os._exit(1)`: a worker then dies with its runner and writes nothing after it. The builder's kill test uses `--procs 1` only; add one with `--procs 2` that asserts no worker pid is alive and no file appears after the kill.
findings.evidence: scripts/kill_resume.py patient: "killed parent 22565 6.4 s after start; workers [22595, 22596, 22597]; alive after kill: [22595, 22596, 22597]"; "orphan workers gone 3.2 s after the kill"; four files written after the parent died (two traces, two partial files); the resume logged "taken over from pid 22565 ... pid 22565 is not alive". Runs race1-3 (resume at once): records and the 8 traces equal the reference's.

findings.problem: Each worker verifies the set itself before its first job (see the verdict), and workers are compared with each other, but the pool's inputs are never compared with the session's, which are the ones in the record key. If the set's files change between the runner's check and the workers' start, the records name hashes the episodes did not run on. The window is seconds, and Stage 1's panels.evaluate has the same gap.
findings.fix: After `tune.Pool(...)` in get_pool: `diff = tune.input_differences(dict(files={f: inputs["files"][f] for f in files}), dict(files={f: pool.inputs["files"].get(f) for f in files}))`, and compare `inputs["freeze"]` with `pool.inputs["freeze"]`; close the pool and raise tune.InputError on a difference.

findings.where: bar.py:2002-2006 and 2013-2014 (`listed` holds `sorted(new)` only, written after the records)
findings.problem: A build check that is killed and resumed lists only the episodes the resuming session ran. A check episode the killed session finished (kept as a partial file, then written into a record) is never listed in dev_episodes.json, and nothing is listed at all if the run dies before its first record. Rule R4: every check episode is listed.

findings.where: bar.py:1698-1716 (_check_rule) and 1780-1781 (no guard on --out before sweep_tmp)
findings.problem: Two holes in the run rule. (a) `set_name not in PREREGISTERED_SETS` matches the three names exactly: a set version the design allows (`F25F9cl.2`, D20) or any other set name needs neither `--task` nor a listed check, so R2 rows on a re-versioned candidate run uncounted and unlisted. (b) `--out` is not checked: a check run with `--out stage2/runs/2026-11-15-75cm` writes a one-seed record into the registered directory and the task's unit then stops on a key mismatch, which pushes the operator to `--supersede` a check; an `--out` under stage1/ or stage2/sets is accepted; and sweep_tmp deletes every `*.tmp` below whatever `--out` names.
findings.fix: (a) Apply the rule to every set but S1 whose set.json does not say `role: "fixture"` (or match the name before the first dot). (b) Refuse an `--out` inside stage1/ or stage2/sets, refuse a check (no --task on such a set) whose `--out` holds a budget.json or lies under stage2/runs/, and sweep only `<out>/budget.json.tmp`, `<out>/<set>/` and `<out>/controls/`.

findings.where: setio.py:220-227 (frozen), relied on by bar.py:1816 and 1649 (work package R's file, not B's)
findings.problem: `manifest_sha256` is copied from set.json and never recomputed from the manifest it names. If a manifest entry is changed together with the file and its entry (by hand or by a builder's fault) while the stored hash is left, the bar accepts the set and writes the old `set_freeze.manifest_sha256` into every record, which is A13's evidence of the freeze a record ran on.
findings.fix: In setio.frozen (or in bar.evaluate and BarWorker before read_inputs) recompute the manifest's hash by the freeze's own definition (the fixture's is `s2io.sha256_json(manifest)`; agree it with work package S) and raise tune.InputError when it differs from the stored one. Since setio.py is in every bar key, land it before state A.

verdict: No blocker found, but six major points should be fixed before code state A, because bar.py is hashed into every record key and rule R4 forbids changing it afterwards. What I saw working, each in the tool's own output: the key holds everything rule R1 lists, with omega and crouch_frac. A changed seed list or a changed input array stops the run with exit 1, prints the differing key fields and leaves every file in the out directory unchanged. A 2-episode smoke with 2 processes, killed with SIGKILL and rerun, gave records equal to an uninterrupted run but for wall times and sessions, byte-identical traces, no duplicate or missing episode, and a ledger equal to the sum of the records' episode wall times. Results did not depend on the worker count. Each spawned worker refuses, before its first job, another thread count, other bar or panel sources, an unfrozen set and a file that differs from its entry or freeze. The runner changed no byte under designlab/stage1 and wrote nothing into stage1/runs, stage2/sets or the worktree. Traces, partial files, locks, temporary files, logs and markers are git-ignored; records, budget.json, COST.md, dev_episodes.json and superseded copies are not. Commit, dirty flag, versions and the per-file source hashes are recorded. The no-loss path reproduces Stage 1: walk/nominal seed 3042 on the S1 view gave trace sha256 7887072a0b0ecaaa... under R2/42@0ms and 048caaae45297c11... under R0@0ms, both equal to the committed records', with episode records equal but for the trace path and wall time. The majors are: the "re-run after a result" label is lost when a superseding run is killed or re-runs a failed episode; a "not run" record is replaced silently and no record can carry A13's "change after a result" label; the chain marks a unit done when episodes failed to run; the dirty flag turns true from the run's own outputs; the crouch behind omega is read from a field no freeze covers; and the chain can drop R0 traces and their hashes unrecorded. Not checked here: a real V0, F25F9 or F25F9cl set (none exists yet), the report module, and the readings and verdict words.
